1	# Arming the standing skills — the detail behind SKILL.md §1
2	
3	Run once, on invoke. SKILL.md carries the one-line summary of each; this is what
4	each one actually means.
5	
6	- **`tickets-zordon`** — read `TICKETS.md` at the repo root. Missing? Say so and
7	  create it on the first ticket, not before. Run its archive step first
8	  (`archive-tickets.sh`; moved rows → commit board + archive together), then
9	  report the open set: `B` bugs, `F` features, `A` agent-found.
10	- **`code-yoda`** — load it (an arm, not a direct invoke: no code-yoda banner); its core is the session's restraint level
11	  (`full` unless the user set another) and governs *what* gets built from here
12	  on. If `PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE` is already in context, the external ponytail
13	  plugin has injected that same core and shows the level in its statusline
14	  badge: code-yoda's own §0 guard then skips the core, and only its three modes
15	  (review · audit · debt) are new. Report the level either way. A suggestion
16	  to run one of its modes, whenever you make one, is a single line in Yoda's
17	  voice, chosen from code-yoda §8 — "Heavy, this diff is. A review from
18	  code-yoda, take you should."
19	- **`codegraph`** — the code map the rest of the skill leans on. Check in order:
20	  `command -v codegraph` → missing? say so and offer
21	  `npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph` (never install silently). Present but
22	  `codegraph status` shows **0 files / 0 nodes** → `codegraph init` (then
23	  `codegraph index` if it was already initialized), **once**. Still 0 after that
24	  means the repo has no indexable source — a docs/skills/config repo — so say
25	  `codegraph: no code to index` and never retry it this session. Already indexed
26	  → `codegraph sync` and move on.
27	- **`live-friday`** — if the repo has a runnable surface (a dev script,
28	  `Cargo.toml`, `CMakeLists.txt`, a `Makefile`, `go.mod`, a Python entry point),
29	  it is armed: the *first* change to that project starts the app or build in the
30	  background and hands over the URL/command **before** the edits, so the user
31	  watches it run instead of waiting on a reply. Nothing runnable → say
32	  `live-friday: nothing to launch` once and drop it. Never auto-launch
33	  simulators, migrations or deploys.
34	- **`watch-cortana`** — on **Claude Code**, confirm the hooks are wired
35	  (`statusLine` runs `usage-watch … -Mode probe`, a `Stop` hook runs
36	  `-Mode gate`). Not wired → say so in one line and offer to wire it; never wire
37	  it silently. On **every other host** there is no hook that can read the usage %
38	and inject at turn end (cursor and antigravity have turn-end hooks; they have no
39	percentage to give them — see `PLATFORMS.md`), so run
40	  `usage-watch.ps1 -Mode check` / `usage-watch.sh check` once here and report
41	  exactly what it says. It reads a real percentage on codex and reports "no
42	  usage signal on this host" on cursor and antigravity — repeat that verbatim
43	  rather than calling it armed. See that skill's **Other hosts** table.
44	- **`rules-orko`** — run `sh <rules-orko>/scripts/rules-orko.sh show` (Windows:
45	  `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
46	  "<rules-orko>/scripts/rules-orko.ps1" show`; `<rules-orko>` is that skill's
47	  directory, a sibling of this one). It prints the repo's committed rules
48	  (`.skillator/rules.md`) and this user's own (`~/.skillator/rules.md`),
49	  scope-tagged. Read both lists before the first task; every line binds the
50	  session as if the user had just typed it. A global rule contradicting a
51	  project rule is **asked** - one `AskUserQuestion` per clash, before the work
52	  it touches - never settled by you (`rules-orko/references/clashes.md`). Report
53	  the counts in the active-set line: `rules-orko: 2 project · 1 global`; both
54	  files absent → `rules-orko: none`. From here on, a standing rule the user
55	  states ("from now on", "always", "never", "in this repo") routes to
56	  `rules-orko` and is on disk before the next tool call.
57	- **`tiers`** (F39) — resolve tier → model for this host once per session, so
58	  `build-jarvis` never has to ask which model. Read `.skillator/tiers.local.md`:
59	  - missing, or its `host:` is not this host → write it: `deep`, `build` and
60	    `cheap` each set to the **first** slug in this host's column of
61	    `PLATFORMS.md` § Role tiers (Claude Code: `fable` / `opus` / `sonnet`, the
62	    Agent tool's `model` values; codex: `gpt-6-astra/high` / `gpt-6-astra/medium`
63	    / `gpt-6-astra/low`), a model the user named in this session winning over
64	    the column;
65	  - present → keep its models, drop every `down:` line not dated today.
66	  The shape (`host:`, `deep:`, `build:`, `cheap:`, `written:`, `down:` lines) is
67	  `skills/build-jarvis/references/grade.md` § The tiers file. The file is local to
68	  this machine and account: make sure the repo's `.gitignore` carries
69	  `.skillator/*.local.md` (append the line if missing; a repo with no
70	  `.gitignore` gets one with that line). Report `tiers deep=<m> build=<m>
71	  cheap=<m>`, plus `(<m> down)` for any model marked down today. Nothing is
72	  probed: a model that turns out unavailable is marked down by build-jarvis at
73	  dispatch, which retries one tier lower.
74	  On **Claude Code** also check that `build-jarvis`'s `UserPromptSubmit` route
75	  hook is wired (`build-jarvis/references/route-hook.md`); not wired → say so in
76	  one line and offer it, never wire it silently.
77	- **Upstream watch** (F23c, F29) — only in a repo that has
78	  `skills/design-arwen/UPSTREAM.md` (skillator itself); anywhere else skip it
79	  silently, because those tickets belong on skillator's board, not the user's.
80	  Run `sh practice/scripts/upstream-check.sh --daily` (Windows:
81	  `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
82	  practice/scripts/upstream-check.ps1 -Daily`). `--daily` makes it a no-op after
83	  the first finished run of the day; the stamp is
84	  `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/skillator/upstream-check.day`, shared by
85	  every worktree. Also run `sh skills/code-yoda/upstream-check.sh --daily`
86	  (Windows: the `.ps1` beside it, `-Daily`) — code-yoda's manifest, same
87	  output shape, its own stamp. Act on the output of both:
88	  - `skipped:` or exit 0: nothing to do.
89	  - each `changed <name> <old>..<new> <url>` line (exit 1, and also exit 2,
90	    because one failed row does not hide another's change): look for an open
91	    (`[ ]` or `[~]`) ticket line in `TICKETS.md` that names both `<name>` and
92	    `<new>`. If there is one, it is already logged. If not, take a number with
93	    `sh practice/scripts/next-id.sh A` and add
94	    `- [ ] A<n> — absorb <name> <old>..<new> into <skill> (<url>)`, `<skill>`
95	    being the one whose manifest reported it (`design-arwen`, or `code-yoda` for
96	    `ponytail`). The procedure is in that skill's `UPSTREAM.md`.
97	  - each `error` line (exit 2): report it in the active-set line as
98	    `upstreams: check failed (<name>)`. Never call a failed check unchanged. No
99	    stamp is written, so the next session retries it.
100	
101	  This is detection and a ticket, never an edit to the skill. Absorbing is a
102	  normal ticket that someone takes on purpose.
103	
104	Then state the active set in **one line** — not a feature tour:
105	
106	```
107	grayskull-power: board 3 open (B2, F7, A1) · codegraph 412 files indexed · code-yoda full · live-friday armed (npm run dev) · watch-cortana armed at 92% · rules-orko: 2 project · 1 global · tiers deep=fable build=opus cheap=sonnet
108	```
109	
110	The banner is printed at the top of the reply, before any of this. It fires
111	**once per session**, on invoke — not on every routed request.
112	
113	---
114	
115	# Persist it for this project (once, then never again)
116	
117	Activation should survive the session and the host. Every one of these CLIs
118	already reads an always-on instruction file from the repo root — that is the
119	carrier, no hook required.
120	
121	On the **first** invoke in a repo, write these four small files and say so in
122	one line. If `.skillator/grayskull.md` already exists, activation is already
123	persisted: skip this whole step silently.
124	
125	**`.skillator/grayskull.md`** — the single source of truth:
126	
127	```markdown
128	# grayskull-power is ON for this project
129	
130	Load and follow `skillator:grayskull-power` for all work here, before
131	anything else. Claude Code: `Skill` tool; Antigravity: `/grayskull-power`;
132	Pi: `/skill:grayskull-power`; Codex/Cursor: read that skill's `SKILL.md`.
133	Print its banner once per session, then route per table.
134	
135	Standing rules:
136	- `TICKETS.md` is the board — `skillator:tickets-zordon` owns it.
137	- Reproduce before fixing; map with `codegraph` first.
138	- Before every commit: regression sweep, then `/code-review`
139	  (`code-review:code-review`) on the staged diff. `skillator:audit-sherlock`
140	  is the whole-app sweep — pre-release, handover, rot — never per-commit,
141	  never inside an implementer.
142	- Staged work runs to the end, no stop between stages. Six stops: a
143	  destructive op, a security-sensitive action, a side effect outside this
144	  worktree (merge, push, publish), the 7-day limit at 90%, a scope-contract
145	  breach, a failed repro. Else log a `Ruling:` in the run file.
146	  `skillator:relay-morpheus` owns `.skillator/run.md`, updated before
147	  dispatch, never after.
148	- One task per fresh implementer, own prompt, no session history —
149	  `skillator:tasks-sentinels` runs that loop. Same-file tasks do not fan out.
150	- Usage watch — before each non-trivial step run
151	  `<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh check`
152	  (Windows: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
153	  "<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.ps1" -Mode check`).
154	  It prints `HANDOFF NOW` plus an order — follow it. Claude Code's `Stop`
155	  hook does this already; skip it.
156	```
157	
158	Write that block **verbatim**, with exactly one substitution — `<SKILL_DIR>`,
159	which occurs twice (once for `.sh`, once for `.ps1`). Nothing else in the block
160	varies per repo.
161	
162	`<SKILL_DIR>` is the directory that contains grayskull-power's own `SKILL.md`:
163	
164	- **Normally** — the skill is installed outside the repo — write its **absolute**
165	  path, forward slashes, no trailing slash. e.g.
166	  `C:/Users/me/.claude/plugins/skillator/skills/grayskull-power`.
167	- **If that directory is inside the repo being activated** (skillator itself,
168	  dogfooding), write it **relative to the repo root** instead —
169	  `skills/grayskull-power` — so the file stays correct for every clone.
170	
171	Leave the `/../watch-cortana/…` tail exactly as written; do **not** pre-normalise
172	the `/../` away. The check at `practice/scripts/check-grayskull-sync.sh` compares
173	the live `.skillator/grayskull.md` against this block on precisely that rule, so
174	a hand-tidied path reads as drift.
175	
176	The path must resolve to a real `usage-watch.sh`. In any repo that is *not*
177	skillator, a repo-relative `skills/watch-cortana/…` does not exist — that is why
178	the absolute form is the default.
179	
180	Then the three host pointers, **appended** (never overwriting what is there):
181	
182	| File | Read by | Line to append |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
185	| `AGENTS.md` | Codex, Cursor | `Read and follow ./.skillator/grayskull.md before any work in this repo.` |
186	| `GEMINI.md` | Antigravity | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
187	
188	Create a file only if it is missing; if it exists, append the line only when it
189	isn't already present. Three near-identical pointers is deliberate — each host
190	reads its own name, and a symlink is not portable to Windows.
191	
192	Deactivating is deleting `.skillator/grayskull.md`; the pointers then resolve to
193	nothing and are harmless. Say that once, don't repeat it.

  every worktree. Also run `sh skills/code-yoda/upstream-check.sh --daily`
  (Windows: the `.ps1` beside it, `-Daily`) — code-yoda's manifest, same
  output shape, its own stamp. Act on the output of both:
  - `skipped:` or exit 0: nothing to do.
  - each `changed <name> <old>..<new> <url>` line (exit 1, and also exit 2,
    because one failed row does not hide another's change): look for an open
    (`[ ]` or `[~]`) ticket line in `TICKETS.md` that names both `<name>` and
    `<new>`. If there is one, it is already logged. If not, take a number with
    `sh practice/scripts/next-id.sh A` and add
    `- [ ] A<n> — absorb <name> <old>..<new> into <skill> (<url>)`, `<skill>`
    being the one whose manifest reported it (`design-arwen`, or `code-yoda` for
    `ponytail`). The procedure is in that skill's `UPSTREAM.md`.
  - each `error` line (exit 2): report it in the active-set line as
    `upstreams: check failed (<name>)`. Never call a failed check unchanged. No
    stamp is written, so the next session retries it.

  This is detection and a ticket, never an edit to the skill. Absorbing is a
  normal ticket that someone takes on purpose.

Then state the active set in **one line** — not a feature tour:

```
grayskull-power: board 3 open (B2, F7, A1) · codegraph 412 files indexed · code-yoda full · live-friday armed (npm run dev) · watch-cortana armed at 92% · rules-orko: 2 project · 1 global · tiers deep=fable build=opus cheap=sonnet
```

The banner is printed at the top of the reply, before any of this. It fires
**once per session**, on invoke — not on every routed request.

---

# Persist it for this project (once, then never again)

Activation should survive the session and the host. Every one of these CLIs
already reads an always-on instruction file from the repo root — that is the
carrier, no hook required.

On the **first** invoke in a repo, write these four small files and say so in
one line. If `.skillator/grayskull.md` already exists, activation is already
persisted: skip this whole step silently.

**`.skillator/grayskull.md`** — the single source of truth:

```markdown
# grayskull-power is ON for this project

Load and follow `skillator:grayskull-power` for all work here, before
anything else. Claude Code: `Skill` tool; Antigravity: `/grayskull-power`;
Pi: `/skill:grayskull-power`; Codex/Cursor: read that skill's `SKILL.md`.
Print its banner once per session, then route per table.

Standing rules:
- `TICKETS.md` is the board — `skillator:tickets-zordon` owns it.
- Reproduce before fixing; map with `codegraph` first.
- Before every commit: regression sweep, then `/code-review`
  (`code-review:code-review`) on the staged diff. `skillator:audit-sherlock`
  is the whole-app sweep — pre-release, handover, rot — never per-commit,
  never inside an implementer.
- Staged work runs to the end, no stop between stages. Six stops: a
  destructive op, a security-sensitive action, a side effect outside this
  worktree (merge, push, publish), the 7-day limit at 90%, a scope-contract
  breach, a failed repro. Else log a `Ruling:` in the run file.
  `skillator:relay-morpheus` owns `.skillator/run.md`, updated before
  dispatch, never after.
- One task per fresh implementer, own prompt, no session history —
  `skillator:tasks-sentinels` runs that loop. Same-file tasks do not fan out.
- Usage watch — before each non-trivial step run
  `<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh check`
  (Windows: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
  "<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.ps1" -Mode check`).
  It prints `HANDOFF NOW` plus an order — follow it. Claude Code's `Stop`
  hook does this already; skip it.
```

Write that block **verbatim**, with exactly one substitution — `<SKILL_DIR>`,
which occurs twice (once for `.sh`, once for `.ps1`). Nothing else in the block
varies per repo.

`<SKILL_DIR>` is the directory that contains grayskull-power's own `SKILL.md`:

- **Normally** — the skill is installed outside the repo — write its **absolute**
  path, forward slashes, no trailing slash. e.g.
  `C:/Users/me/.claude/plugins/skillator/skills/grayskull-power`.
- **If that directory is inside the repo being activated** (skillator itself,
  dogfooding), write it **relative to the repo root** instead —
  `skills/grayskull-power` — so the file stays correct for every clone.

Leave the `/../watch-cortana/…` tail exactly as written; do **not** pre-normalise
the `/../` away. The check at `practice/scripts/check-grayskull-sync.sh` compares
the live `.skillator/grayskull.md` against this block on precisely that rule, so
a hand-tidied path reads as drift.

The path must resolve to a real `usage-watch.sh`. In any repo that is *not*
skillator, a repo-relative `skills/watch-cortana/…` does not exist — that is why
the absolute form is the default.

Then the three host pointers, **appended** (never overwriting what is there):

| File | Read by | Line to append |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` | Codex, Cursor | `Read and follow ./.skillator/grayskull.md before any work in this repo.` |
| `GEMINI.md` | Antigravity | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |

Create a file only if it is missing; if it exists, append the line only when it
isn't already present. Three near-identical pointers is deliberate — each host
reads its own name, and a symlink is not portable to Windows.

Deactivating is deleting `.skillator/grayskull.md`; the pointers then resolve to
nothing and are harmless. Say that once, don't repeat it.
